neighbours.label: Multiplication by cosine, especially a scalar times math.cos(...) in coordinate calculations.
fire: The particle simulation computes horizontal velocity as speed * math.cos(angle) at each update.
For the circular diagram, the horizontal coordinate is radius * math.cos(theta) relative to the center.
Our game calculates the sideways displacement using distance * math.cos(heading) before moving the character.
In the compact plotting routine, x=r*math.cos(theta) determines each point's horizontal position.
The spherical conversion sets x = r * sin(theta) * cos(phi) for the resulting Cartesian coordinate.
During the rotation, the program evaluates projected_length = length * math.cos(tilt) to determine the visible span.
The geometry solution multiplies the original area by the cosine of the inclination angle.
According to the mechanics exercise, the horizontal force equals the applied force multiplied by the cosine of its angle.
quiet: Each particle update computes horizontal velocity as speed * horizontal_fraction within the simulation.
When drawing the circular diagram, use radius * horizontal_ratio for the horizontal coordinate relative to the center.
Before moving the game character, calculate sideways displacement as distance * direction_fraction.
A compact plotting routine uses x=r*horizontal_ratio to determine each point's horizontal position.
For the spherical conversion, the resulting Cartesian coordinate is x = r * vertical_ratio * horizontal_ratio.
To determine the visible span during rotation, evaluate projected_length = length * projection_ratio.
In the geometry solution, multiply the original area by the given projection factor.
For this mechanics exercise, the horizontal force equals the applied force multiplied by the specified horizontal fraction.
